summary: The KRAS-mutant preclinical combination-response finding is supported within the tested models. Retain a warning about the description: wild-type controls responded to cetuximab alone, and mild monotherapy effects and culture conditions need qualification. The original whole-annotation CONTRADICT verdict remains recorded; it should not be interpreted as disproving the scoped mutant finding.
proposed_scoped_summary: In LS180, LoVo and HCT116 KRAS-mutant colorectal models, cetuximab plus dasatinib reduced proliferation under PDL/laminin culture conditions and inhibited xenograft growth. Cetuximab alone was ineffective in these tested mutant xenografts; dasatinib alone had limited, non-significant tumor-growth effects. SW48 and CaCo2 were wild-type controls sensitive to cetuximab alone. HCT116 showed a more modest combination response. These are preclinical observations, without demonstrated clinical benefit.

findings.explanation: The source supports reduced proliferation and tumor growth under combined cetuximab and dasatinib in the tested LS180, LoVo and HCT116 KRAS-mutant models. This is preclinical evidence, not a claim about all KRAS variants or patient benefit.

SW48 and CaCo2 were cetuximab-sensitive wild-type controls. Their monotherapy response does not contradict the KRAS-mutant combination finding. Wording that extends combination-only efficacy to all five named lines is misleading; the combination experiments described here used the three mutant lines.

The paper reports mild dasatinib growth inhibition in vitro and minimal, non-significant tumor-growth delay in some mutant xenografts. The phrase neither monotherapy had efficacy must not become a universal assertion of no biological effect or a formal synergy claim.

The in-vitro resistance pattern depended on PDL/laminin culture conditions; mutant cells responded differently on plastic or fibronectin. HCT116 had a more modest combination response. Preserve these context limits rather than generalizing to every experimental setting.

Cell lines and mouse xenografts supply no demonstrated patient response or clinical recommendation. The paper proposes further clinical investigation; this overlay does not validate the whole CIViC profile or every KRAS variant.

The supplied methods sequence cell-line DNA; these passages do not independently establish the annotated somatic origin through matched-normal or germline analysis. This remains an evidentiary gap rather than a contradiction.
